title: Whole-model Walsh response atoms
summary: Signed Walsh-8 labels give a cheap 0.6267-BPW direct response map but destroy Qwen3-0.6B language quality.
comparison: Test NLL 14.626 versus BF16 3.311 and plain RTN4 4.242.
limitation: Rejection is for this isotropic atom family on the pilot, not all response codebooks.
next: Learn activation-sensitive codes and composed consumers.

title: NanoQuant-derived binary factor baseline
summary: Pinned ADMM initializer supplies matched real-activation sub-bit factor images and packed direct-reader controls.
comparison: At .55 target BPW, held response squared errors across 16 projections range .0342 to .4810; it is the internal matched adversary, not published NanoQuant quality.
limitation: No published reconstruction/KD stages, complete quality claim or universal speed estimate.
next: Compare full model and native consumers at matched endpoints.

title: Low-rate spectral factors and attention-aware Q fitting
summary: Rank-88 4/4-bit Q factors fit at .53674 BPW; attention-fitted codes trade raw response error for causal quality, and the exact image runs faster than the stronger binary control in paired native tests.
comparison: Initial early-Q response error .08145 versus ADMM binary .09666; attention fit held KL .07776 versus response-refined binary .08164. Paired native speedups 1.114x/1.725x at 1/16 queries.
limitation: Fresh 64-window test removes the quality advantage: NLL 3.61148 versus 3.61078, KL .05807 versus .05278. Single projection only; not matched SOTA.
next: Fit a complete causal map on fresh quantized-producer text before deployment.

title: Spectral rate, calibration and larger-model transfer
summary: Rank/precision and train-window sweeps expose a real low-rate trade on Qwen3-0.6B, but 1.7B does not sustain a spectral quality advantage.
comparison: Early 0.6B Q .53674-BPW error .08145 versus .53906 binary .09666; 1.7B early Q .07042 spectral versus .05385 refitted binary despite fewer spectral bytes.
limitation: Three transferred matrices and four-window continuations do not establish scaling or whole-model quality.
next: Train against larger-model consumer on independent text, with calibration budget controlled.

title: Fixed-right higher rank and radial precision
summary: Increasing frozen-right Q rank or reducing left precision without a new fit does not preserve the attention-trained 4/4 map.
comparison: Frozen-right rank 108 two/four held KL .20130 versus rank 88 .19934 on its seed; attention-trained rank-88 two/four reaches .11290 but 3/4 reaches .09242.
limitation: Rejects these frozen-basis/rate shortcuts, not joint right-code fitting.
next: Choose precision and right basis jointly for causal loss.

title: Jointly adapted lower-bit Q basis
summary: Refitting both factors makes a rank-108 two/four-bit attention image useful at the three/four-byte cap.
comparison: Held KL .09985 versus equal-fit rank-88 two/four .10367; rank-88 three/four still wins .09242 at 1,728 more bytes and fewer terms.
limitation: Original producer, fixed Q only; native latency and model loss not measured.
next: Test new factor bases and extra rank against the stronger three/four control on fresh model loss.

title: Short-vector response codebooks
summary: The all-row codebook shortlist loses rate/response quality to the ADMM-derived factor control; scalar packed-table CPU lowering is much slower than dense VNNI on the same quantized map.
comparison: Three Qwen projections: .882-.891 BPW codebooks have larger held squared error than .771-.773 BPW binary; 14.869 us fresh-table versus 4.665 us dense VNNI on one Bonsai block.
limitation: Rejection applies to this fitted family and scalar CPU reader, not jointly learned codebooks or vectorized hardware.
next: Change shared response structure and fit whole consumers before new kernels.

title: Butterfly and patterned input factors
summary: Learned butterfly transforms and patterned binary input factors reduce selected work, but lose the matched .55-bit response comparison to equally fitted binary factors.
comparison: Pattern arms recover capacity over butterflies but remain behind activation-fitted binary on the measured projections.
limitation: Frozen grammar and calibration scope, not a universal transform lower bound.
next: Co-design reusable input stages and full downstream response rather than accelerate these losing images.

title: Spectral modes and fair binary scale control
summary: Allocating a few real response modes within the same byte budget helps selected binary-factor images; a zero-byte output-scale refit is a stronger universal local control.
comparison: With the same scale refit on both arms, hybrid wins 8 of 16 .55-bit matrices; binary-only scale refit improves all sixteen.
limitation: No uniform advantage, native latency or full-model loss.
next: Allocate residual modes by composed sensitivity and charge their direct runtime.

title: Shared first binary Q/K/V factors
summary: Sharing a first factor improves K/V but worsens Q at matched aggregate .44922 BPW; the wider second factor consumes its saved first-stage work.
comparison: Equal aggregate rate and signed-work comparison against separate binary factors, recorded in shared-qkv.md.
limitation: Only the tested shared architecture and original-producer objectives are rejected.
next: Train the shared map on the complete attention response.

title: Complete sub-bit binary-factor images
summary: Complete .62454/.76000/.89546-BPW packed images account for all body, tied head and norms, but none retains useful language quality. Existing-scale end-to-end fitting partly repairs the .62454 image.
comparison: At .62454 BPW, test NLL 9.65603 after response sweeps and 9.11738 after scale repair versus BF16 3.31076 and scalar RTN4 4.05740 at 4.12635 BPW.
limitation: No full-model native consumer, strong quantizer comparator or acceptable sub-bit language quality.
next: Fit coupled layer-0 V/O and MLP with the quantized tied image and later body in the objective.

title: Original-producer FP16 residual allocation
summary: Rank-8/16 residuals improve every isolated matrix response but make complete-model test loss worse while consuming more bytes.
limitation: Rejects this frozen original-producer quadratic allocation, not all residual training.
next: Select extra bytes by composed model loss.

title: Complete scalar rounding controls
summary: The group-128 two-bit LS scalar control collapses and is a poor benchmark for a superiority claim; four-bit is much better but remains a plain rather than reconstructed quantizer.
comparison: Two-bit 2.12657 BPW test NLL 15.55316; four-bit 4.12635 BPW test NLL 4.05740 versus BF16 3.31076.
limitation: This classifies the two-bit construction on Qwen3-0.6B, not scalar quantization generally.
next: Use GPTQ/QuIP#/NanoQuant-class matched quality and rate before a SOTA claim.

title: Layer-0 coupled V/O and MLP repair
summary: Fresh substitutions identify a large damaged layer-0 prefix and non-additive V/O-to-MLP interaction; binary Q/K can remain while exact V/O and MLP restore most local loss.
comparison: Restoring layer 0 cuts 16-window prefix NLL 13.014 to 7.626 but costs .40830 whole-model BPW; narrow V/O plus original MLP test/validation NLL 10.579/8.819.
limitation: Exact restoration is not sub-bit; single/two MLP projection restorations do not suffice.
next: Fit compressed coupled V/O, gate, up and down on quantized producer.

title: Paid MLP scale and gold gain fitting
summary: Refitting already-paid input/output scales and choosing down/O gains on gold labels improves damaged-prefix loss without new image bytes or factor work.
comparison: Input/output scales lower held post-MLP error .65752 to .62089; down gain lowers 18-window test NLL 11.32575 to 9.54966 and joint O gain lowers another test panel 9.58521 to 8.75417.
limitation: Prefix has original downstream layers and remains badly damaged; gains transfer poorly to complete image.
next: Fit gains and factor codes through quantized tied and downstream layers.

title: Reduced-rank MLP response repair
summary: A covariance-aware rank-32 paid FP16 residual repairs the earlier coefficient-truncation negative on the same frozen hidden responses.
comparison: Held post-MLP error .65752 to .61904 at rank 32 versus .66098 for coefficient truncation.
limitation: Costs 264,192 extra bytes and 131,072 terms/token; model loss and native time not measured.
next: Compare with zero-byte scale refits on quantized-producer model loss.

title: MLP response-selected sign and gain shortcuts
summary: Improved frozen-hidden endpoint error and train-selected gain pairs fail to select the best held NLL image.
comparison: Two-sweep down signs lower endpoint error .83064 to .82140 but worsen six-window test NLL 11.56619 to 11.83990; complete gain train choice 2/1.5 loses to 2/1.75 on held panels.
limitation: Rejects these response and tiny-grid selectors, not jointly trained MLP codes.
next: Train broader complete-model gold/teacher continuation.

title: Shared tied head and embedding mixed image
summary: One sub-bit image serves input embeddings and output head; mixed exact/codebook/RTN4 rows win only when both consumers propagate through the model.
comparison: At .893824 tied BPW, shared replacement test/validation NLL 4.32659/4.96719 versus .895325 exact-row 4.36930/4.98173; head-only ranking reverses.
limitation: All other body weights original; no native reader or strong SOTA comparator.
next: Fit rare rows and both consumers on larger fresh model panels.

title: Tied rare-row low-rank corrections
summary: Unweighted rank-16 residual worsens head NLL despite lower logit RMS; curvature-only rank-eight and signed rank-64 mixed residuals also lose to frequent exact rows.
comparison: Unweighted rank-16 NLL 5.945 versus K256 alone 5.795; at .886111 BPW curvature rank eight NLL 4.932 versus 2,560-exact .895325-BPW 4.629.
limitation: Fixed original final-hidden inputs; no quantized embedding propagation.
next: Fit gold-token and occurrence objectives through both tied consumers.

title: Exact tied-row allocation and joint rank-eight fit
summary: Occurrence-weighted rank-eight fitting improves same-budget NLL/embedding error; exact row selection by embedding error improves KL with little NLL change.
comparison: Same 128 train inputs: rank-eight occurrence NLL 4.749 versus curvature-only 4.912 at .886111 BPW; embedding-selected exact rows KL 1.00130 versus frequent 1.06488 at .895325 BPW.
limitation: Frequent exact rows still win NLL; 64 held original-hidden positions and no native time.
next: Fit on independent head data and measure propagated shared-image loss.

title: Gold-selected tied exact-row overfit
summary: Exact greedy selected-set optimization does not repair the gold-row selection failure on 128 head inputs.
comparison: Gold-row held NLL 4.692; joint-set greedy 4.695 versus frequent exact rows 4.629 at identical .895325 BPW.
limitation: Finite candidate pool and small original-hidden panel, not a general greedy theorem.
next: Increase independent training data and learn rare responses instead of reshuffling exact IDs.

title: Tied head frequency buckets and code-label shortcut
summary: Paid frequency buckets lower fixed-input held NLL with a small rate increase, but existing code labels cannot replace the extra frequency IDs.
comparison: Bucket NLL 4.38285 versus matched global 4.40296 at +56,988 bytes; code-label choice 4.48083 versus global 4.40296 on its matched panel.
limitation: Teacher KL slightly worsens for bucket fit, no quantized-embedding propagation or native timing.
next: Test whether bucket gain survives full-model tied use and whether routing cost is worth it.

title: Shared narrow GQA value observer
summary: A rank-28 shared V basis and two paid output decoders carry narrow coordinates through cache and both attention heads.
comparison: At .53060 V/O BPW versus independent .53652, held post-O error .37889/.32619 versus .39579/.35247 at layers 0/14; layer-0 single-layer test NLL 4.90511 versus 8.73188.
limitation: Layer-14 NLL slightly reverses, no complete-model native reader or simultaneous all-layer quality.
next: Jointly fit upstream and both downstream consumers on fresh text; price narrow cache and paid O.

title: Narrow V rank allocation, pruning and refit
summary: Equal-byte rank allocation and 192-coordinate causal pruning beat uniform frozen allocations; paid code refitting and ridge recover further post-O quality.
comparison: Selected 192-coordinate .466797-BPW images held post-O .385779/.330364 versus equal-rate uniform .407794/.340384 at original producers; quantized-producer ridge layer-14 .336551 to .303868.
limitation: Fresh layer-0 validation NLL reverses selected-rank advantage; quantized-producer uniform/selected converge and original V/O remains competitive.
next: Fit new right bases and codes with broader complete-model loss before native layout choice.

title: Frozen V allocation and scale-only selection limits
summary: Non-prefix mask exchanges barely improve the best prefix, robust train-window weighting cannot fix a fresh NLL reversal, and frozen group-gain refits have little held benefit.
comparison: Non-prefix layer-0 .391723 to .390890; layer-14 exact same mask; paid group gains .336551 to .336186 while held oracle can reach .312639.
limitation: Only frozen masks, scales and inspected train distributions are rejected.
next: Learn basis, producer and target jointly rather than shuffle old coordinates.

title: Narrow V cache and output layouts
summary: Packed unequal-rank layouts and selected-output column preservation expose a smaller paid V/O rate and fewer logical terms.
comparison: Ten preserved head groups with two-bit transfer cost .428472 V/O BPW and error .413157/.375237 versus separately rounded rank-256 .454834 and .590752/.631886.
limitation: Original .530599 image remains more accurate; line requests and factor terms are not native latency.
next: Measure complete two-stage V/O/cache consumers, then co-train output codes.

title: Frozen shared-output factor shortcuts
summary: Independent low-rank output rounding, single-group swaps, wrong-head attention substitution and paired-difference rank do not provide a good cheap frozen decoder.
comparison: Rounded rank-256 error .590752/.631886; rank-24 difference changes paid output .027455/.017171 for four saved dots; partner-attention substitution raises layer-0 error .413157 to .456104.
limitation: Real rank-256 is useful; rejects these two-bit rounding and frozen-head approximations only.
next: Co-fit paid shared output basis, both attention paths and value codes.

title: One-byte narrow V cache and integer consumer
summary: E4M3 halves paid narrow-V cache to 224 bytes/token with little original-producer error; signed-byte labels permit exact conserved-count integer dots and late scale factoring.
comparison: E4M3 held error .379186/.326527; 4,095-count int8 .378890/.326401 at layers 0/14, plus 432 FP16 metadata bytes/layer.
limitation: Native append/count/dot/O and quantized-producer NLL not measured; cache format is not weight BPW.
next: Compare full fused int8, E4M3 and nibble readers at occupied context.

title: Frozen byte-cache scale and affine fitting
summary: Training only frozen E4M3 group scales or affine int8 code shifts buys negligible or reversed held quality at extra work.
comparison: E4M3 causal scales .37918583 to .37917539 layer 0 but .32652724 to .32653087 layer 14; affine int8 layer 14 .32640123 to .32643822.
limitation: Narrow frozen scale/grid objective, not a negative for joint producer-consumer training.
next: Learn new value codes and basis on quantized-producer loss.

title: Half-byte V code and paid decoder fitting
summary: Coordinate steps, endpoint code, paid O refits and learned byte LUT reduce the half-byte cache error while keeping narrow values direct.
comparison: Layer-14 half-byte error .365386 to .334500 with paid O refit, then .330807 with LUT, versus equally refitted E4M3 .325434.
limitation: Still loses E4M3 held quality; LUT adds 4,032 static bytes and two dot passes, no native or model loss.
next: Co-train V basis/cache/O against quantized-producer language loss.

title: Frozen V palette and mixed-bit shortcuts
summary: Sharing the learned byte palette and spending two equal-byte fifth-bit coordinate pairs do not improve the frozen nibble image.
comparison: Shared pairs layer-14 error .335839 versus uniform nibble .334500 with more table bytes; mixed-rate .334550 versus parent .334500.
limitation: Only these frozen code/decoder and original-producer fits.
next: Change the basis and consumers instead of reallocating frozen labels.

title: Exact conserved-mass V dot and sparse overflow
summary: A 4,095-unit count map lets packed narrow V labels remain integer through causal attention; sparse high-count corrections avoid a second dense byte dot.
comparison: Correction products 1.071m/1.142m versus 58.950m in second dense pass on layers 0/14; integer responses and quality unchanged.
limitation: Count formation, irregular gathers, paid O and native latency not measured.
next: Time complete fused reader against two-dot and E4M3 alternatives.

title: Headwise count precision and nibble mass dots
summary: Train-selected 255/4,095-unit head allocation and direct packed-nibble mass dots reduce estimated dot slots at controlled output error.
comparison: At 1e-4 train rounding budget, fifteen/four 255-unit heads reduce modeled four-lane slots 50.2%/12.3% at held errors 8.79e-5/6.06e-5; three-nibble full-count map cuts modeled slots 36.1%/41.1% against byte dots.
limitation: No native count/list/dot/O timing; frozen nibble cache still loses E4M3 quality.
next: Train code and mass precision together; time entire consumer.

title: Value-aware rounded mass and cheap phase policies
summary: Exact phase event search improves a frozen count map; a cached byte sketch and 16-phase policy capture part of the gain without dense per-query code projections.
comparison: Inspected sketch policy error .00019788/.00094393 versus fixed phase .00035732/.00122964 at layers 0/14; exact search .000464 to .000281 on sampled layer-14 rows.
limitation: Append sketch/query scans and native cost not measured; even chosen phase may miss complete-layer eligibility.
next: Co-learn the phase selector, sketch and V/O codes on fresh quantized-producer text.

title: Frozen low-rank, fixed-phase and one-digit shortcuts
summary: A fixed 15-unit phase cannot meet the declared 1e-4 budget for any frozen head; low-rank phase metrics remain costly and inaccurate.
comparison: Best one-head fixed-phase train errors .00010574/.00089142; rank-one phase score worsens layer-14 held response .000464 to .000543.
limitation: Applies to frozen codes and selected budgets, not learned phase-aware codes.
next: Learn cheap query state jointly with the cache, not another frozen phase sweep.

title: Sparse list and count-work illusions
summary: Fewer logical high/low products, compacted zeros or lower-radix counts often fail once issued lanes, support construction and shared physical reads enter the bill.
comparison: Prefix radix 256 versus compact radix 128 costs 2.229m versus 2.211m layer-0 four-lane slots; optimal rounding saves only 1.32%/.96% complete slots; sparse low compaction saves 4.1% layer-0 slots before compaction.
limitation: These are frozen 256-token slot/read models, not GPU timing or universal lower bounds.
next: Price fused count prep, append, cache gathers and paid O at occupied contexts.

title: Temporal and rowwise V entropy coding
summary: Exact canonical Huffman and independently appendable row streams compress frozen narrow-V labels; absolute layer-0 rows remove the suffix-score dependency.
comparison: Layer-0 absolute row 92.851 versus static nibble 112 bytes/token; layer-14 difference row 101.713 versus 112, with exact code and integer response.
limitation: Native Huffman parser, append, mass scan, O and model quality not measured.
next: Time one/two-parser absolute and difference readers with actual shared physical traffic.

title: Frozen V differential and parser dead ends
summary: Simple temporal three-bit differences, fixed-five-bit zero runs, paged coordinate streams and phrase rows lose to static nibble or the row Huffman reader after paying append metadata.
comparison: Layer-0 delta 114.845 versus 112 static bytes/token; paged optimum 125.219/121.898 and phrase optimum 124.850/123.154 on layers 0/14, both above 112.
limitation: Bounded frozen grammars, not entropy limits on jointly trained labels.
next: Use appendable key rows or retrain repeat-rich labels.

title: Sparse V row traffic and mixed streams
summary: Per-head zero masses rarely remove a row shared by sixteen heads, and mixed absolute/difference coding saves little storage while adding parses.
comparison: Only 7/131,584 layer-0 causal pairs have all-head zero mass; eight group streams raise cold lines 10.8% versus one; mixed layer-14 saves 1.052 bytes/token but adds 16.6% parses.
limitation: CPU cold-line/parser model on frozen rows, no native time.
next: Measure one-parser complete reader or co-train group-union support.

title: Exact V dictionary and signed-byte grouped reader
summary: Repeated layer-0 producer inputs allow whole-row signed-byte V deduplication and a one-byte append ID; selective duplicate grouping plus paired-head differences reduces byte-dot row uses.
comparison: Layer-0 cache 125.273 versus 224 bytes/key; grouped byte products 36.14m versus raw 58.95m plus correction work; paired rows 1,290,736 to 1,081,333 over four windows.
limitation: Layer 14 unique rows bypass indexing; histogram, append, O and native latency unpaid.
next: Build one fused token-ID append/count/paired byte-dot/O reader, not isolated logical-work claims.

title: Static GQA value-head direction
summary: A static B-first order saves corrections, but per-query orientation buys too little before selector/routing cost.
comparison: Layer-0 paired-label B-first corrections 76,826 to 69,010; dynamic minimum removes 4,050 more, only .334% of 32-padded byte-dot uses.
limitation: Rejects dynamic orientation as an isolated feature on inspected windows, not a jointly routed reader.
next: Price fused static B-first grouped reader.

title: Causal first-seen V dictionary merging
summary: Reducing the exact dictionary to 128 frozen centers damages response quality too much for the saved bytes and labels.
comparison: Layer-0 bytes/key 125.273 to 112.805 but held error .378889 to .403381; layer-14 .326373 to .434637.
limitation: Fixed first-seen centers/nearest key-local paid-O assignment, not a limit on jointly learned dictionaries.
next: Train causal centers and cheap assignment with producer.

title: Signed-byte two-head correction schedule
summary: One base dot and a signed difference, bounded high lists and padded high-byte correction expose a direct GQA reader with exact integer responses.
comparison: Ideal low-byte products fall 15.7%/16.4% at layers 0/14 versus two dense dots; four-row padded high lists 99,040/84,220 versus 32-padding 513,600/510,400.
limitation: Correction/list preparation and native whole path not measured.
next: Compare fused short high-byte dot with scalar correction on real cache.

title: RoPE key-orbit and stationary recurrence barriers
summary: A generic fixed post-RoPE narrow linear decoder or stationary query recurrence does not cheaply carry a rank-one key through all active positions.
comparison: Pinned first-column heads excite all 64 RoPE planes and require 128 cached coordinates or 128 stationary oscillator states under named exact grammars; best rank-28 isotropic rotated-key projection retains .380/.444 energy.
limitation: Restricted unrestricted-query/fixed-linear or stationary recurrence claims, not a limit on learned approximate position-aware scores.
next: Fit selected planes and producer with both causal heads.

title: RoPE-compatible selected-plane score geometry
summary: Whole-plane masks commute with RoPE and preserve direct narrow score maps; causal fitting improves fixed-budget text attention far more than weight covariance masks.
comparison: At 112 planes, covariance mask held KL 1.460/2.782 versus causal-fitted .367/.489, then finite exchanges .301/.448 and shared gains .229977/.343686 at layers 0/14.
limitation: Original-producer attention only; selected-row Q/K images, native timing and model loss not measured.
next: Fit paid Q/K signs, mask, gains and norm against quantized-producer downstream loss.

title: Paid selected-plane Q/K and sparse normalization
summary: Paid binary Q/K images can use selected planes, existing affine slots and unused padded cache lines; positive sparse raw K rows approximate full RMSNorm while saving output terms.
comparison: 128-plane full-norm held KL .252318/.308216; 16-extra-row sparse .253286/.325664, train-exchanged rows .246907/.308927 at unchanged 512-byte padded cache.
limitation: Four original-producer windows and CPU map; native time, BF16 norm equivalence and quantized-upstream language loss not measured.
next: Jointly learn paid K row support, Q/K codes and score observer.

title: Frozen key norm Gram and naive sketch limits
summary: Frozen paid K missing-row Grams have full rank; cheap dense Gram or naive sampled-row energy does not reproduce the denominator across layers.
comparison: Exact Gram needs 800 forms/204,800 terms; 32 sampled rows save 26.6% K factor terms but layer-0 held KL .263253 to .304696.
limitation: Exact bound is for frozen factor-coordinate quadratic; trained positive sparse rows remain promising.
next: Train support on finite causal loss, not norm reconstruction error.

title: Post-RoPE translation gauge and one-byte cache
summary: Post-RoPE constant-key translation cancels from softmax; centering the paid selected-score cache supports a one-byte key representation.
comparison: Centered int8 selected groups lower layer-0 held KL .309766 to .260361 while padded cache shrinks 512 to 256 bytes/token/layer.
limitation: Layer-14 BF16 rounding of the exact quotient reverses its tiny KL gain; native read and model loss not measured.
next: Co-fit centering with paid query/key labels on quantized producers.

title: Direct nibble K and shared three-dot score
summary: Signed-nibble K rows use 128 bytes/token with a two-dot integer query; sharing one head base cuts score products by a quarter and gives a small native local speedup.
comparison: Three-dot versus four-dot held KL .278608/.334929 versus .275431/.332396; native score/softmax 17.101 to 15.588 us but append/prep boundary only 30.524 to 29.155 us at 1,024 keys.
limitation: No paid K producer/value/O timing or quality-matched SOTA win; quantized-upstream NLL not measured.
next: Train Q/K labels for complete downstream attention; compare full native boundary.

title: Nibble K rate and conditional query controls
summary: Mixed three/four-bit keys save cache bytes and exact conditional shared-query rounding slightly improves held KL at unchanged three key dots.
comparison: Mixed 112 versus 128 bytes/token scores .282826/.345606; fifteen-choice shared fit KL .278608 to .278049 and .334929 to .333448.
limitation: Rounding costs up to 3,840 candidate evaluations/query/layer; native selector/producer and model loss unpaid.
next: Fit cheaper causal query preparation and paid key codes together.

title: Frozen query precision and sharing dead ends
summary: Single-dot scale policies, sparse second dots, covariance selectors, dynamic bases and two-dot affine sharing do not supply a cheaper quality-matched frozen reader.
comparison: Layer-14 single-dot covariance scale worsens KL .362763 to .476919; sparse 24-coordinate correction .338124 still loses full second dot .332397; dynamic base deployable selector worsens .334929 to .335671.
limitation: Bounded frozen labels and selector grammars, not jointly learned scores.
next: Change producer and fit causal observer, not another frozen selector.

title: Direct temporal K difference scores and entropy streams
summary: Temporal nibble differences can feed exact two-head scores directly; Huffman four/eight-row streams reduce frozen layer-14 storage further.
comparison: Layer-14 32-key direct difference 106.737 versus static mixed 112 bytes/token; four-row Huffman 96.837, eight-row 95.669, with exact score recurrence.
limitation: Layer 0 loses static on bytes; append, parser, scan, K producer and native timing unpaid.
next: Time fixed segment reader and jointly learn independently decodable K differences.

title: Frozen K predictor and selector overhead
summary: Second differences, per-coordinate alphabets, two-bit escapes, paired dictionaries and adaptive segment selection fail rate or practical-work tests on frozen keys.
comparison: Layer-14 second-order row 125.561 versus first-order 105.521 bytes/token; coordinate seven-symbol held oracle 106.593 exceeds Huffman 96.837; two-bit delta 121,260 versus 109,299 bytes.
limitation: Only named frozen grammars and charged metadata; not a bound on learned K codes.
next: Keep fixed first-difference reader or train new temporal labels.

title: RoPE commuting phase and finite-cell fitting
summary: Fixed Q/K basis transformations commuting with all RoPE positions reduce to one complex multiplier per plane; phase changes rounding cells without changing real unrounded scores.
comparison: Checked synthetic rounded two-head case KL .038051 to .017398; dynamic-max synthetic KL .014947 to .005113, convex bracket tightens to .00000136.
limitation: Synthetic/fixed-step or numerical search; Qwen held attention and native phase/append cost not measured.
next: Fit phase and labels on quantized-upstream Qwen causal text.

title: Packed paired Q/K score radix bound
summary: A single exact paired signed-nibble dot needs radix at least 3,099 on the full 32-coordinate cube, exceeding signed-byte query lanes; the two-key quotient barely saves entropy.
comparison: Every smaller positive radix has a two-head score collision; at 256 keys common translation saves under one millionth bit/group relative to base-15 coding.
limitation: Exact unrestricted cube and named single-dot decoder only, not learned approximate codes.
next: Retain practical two/three-dot score programs or change the representation family.

title: Layer-0 token-ID paid projection reuse
summary: At original Qwen3-0.6B layer 0, repeated token IDs have bit-identical QKV inputs; pre-RoPE Q/K and V projections can be reused while rotation and position append still run.
comparison: Across twelve windows 1,326/3,072 repeated IDs save 304,152,576 of 704,643,072 V right-factor terms; four-window Q/K reuse skips 732,168,192 of 1,644,167,168 factor terms.
limitation: Layer 14 token IDs do not imply same inputs; rotated values cannot be reused, and native lookup/table/append cost not measured.
next: Price fused layer-0 Q/K/V append and score path.

title: Post-O head-rate allocation
summary: An exact finite sixteen-head quadratic reallocates frozen 2/3-bit Q precision for the downstream attention output.
comparison: At .40778 BPW, train-selected mask lowers held post-O squared error .024280 to .022787 versus an attention-KL selected mask at equal bytes/work.
limitation: Frozen two-bit/three-bit Q arms and inspected original-producer data; no fresh model NLL or native mixed-bit reader.
next: Select with fresh quantized-producer model loss, then price mixed-bit execution.

title: Strong quantization comparator map
summary: The frontier report separates NanoQuant PTQ, LittleBit/ParetoQ QAT, QTIP/QuIP# structured PTQ, and direct-consumer CPU/GPU controls with their different model, rate and compute denominators.
comparison: Published Llama-2/Llama-3 quality and CUDA/CPU times are context, not a matched Kelana win.
limitation: No same-model strong SOTA head-to-head or quality-matched native comparison has been completed.
next: Reproduce strong competitors on the same model, data, compute budget and measured native boundary.

title: Tied factor head-coordinate covariance
summary: Covariance-weighted rank-eight residual improves raw head loss but loses after the matched rare-logit calibration and harms the embedding consumer.
comparison: At .886111 BPW, calibrated held NLL 4.74903 to 4.81208 and embedding RMS .45853 to .46017 for alpha one.
limitation: Only the sampled head metric, rank-eight sketch and 32-position calibration are rejected.
next: Use more disjoint calibration and propagated tied-model gold loss.

title: Frozen K/V conditional entropy tables
summary: One frozen cache supplies too little predictive information for a second conditional Huffman table to beat separate static/entropy-coded layouts.
comparison: Best layer-0 V condition saves 886 bytes/1,024 tokens but costs 114.35 bytes/token versus static nibble 112 and group Huffman 103.36; layer-14 conditional streams grow.
limitation: Frozen independently learned K/V labels and same-token two-table grammar only.
next: Jointly train K/V labels and causal/post-O consumers with the side decode charged.

title: Direct packed binary factor readers
summary: Bitplane dots, half-orbit response tables, partitioned byte tables and a routed quartet consume the existing paid sign factors without an int4 intermediate.
comparison: Routed quartet cuts signed updates to 45.12% for an up projection before 294,912 routes; balanced two-subtable program needs sixteen rather than 128 table entries but doubles lookup and row-add work.
limitation: No matched complete native reader or full-model A7 quality result; operation counts are not speed.
next: Compare complete packed two-factor gfx1151 readers with table prep, scale and rank traffic charged.

title: A7 masked byte response and sparse carry
summary: One mask bit per four-sign byte-table entry corrects every full-domain A7 response; a sparse carry pass can defer exceptional sign updates.
comparison: Only .626-.886% of 25.166m paid selections/layer need correction; sparse pass revisits 1.069m-1.526m sign quartets instead of masking all uses.
limitation: All byte lookups still pay mask traffic; no native whole-reader comparison or model loss.
next: Time masked-byte, sparse-carry, int16 quartet and two-sign byte readers end to end.

title: Frozen A7 static four-sign byte admission
summary: Most observed individual quartet tables fit bytes, but a uniformly byte-safe fixed rank-table position is rare; centering adds too many corrections.
comparison: Only 5-18% of rank positions are byte-safe across 64 inputs; centered admission rises to 30-47 of 96 positions but costs 6.97m-7.31m rank corrections/layer.
limitation: Named static admission/frozen code grammar, not the masked-byte exact map or jointly trained code.
next: Compare uniform or masked complete readers before changing admission rules.

title: Dynamic rank-group A7 center
summary: Input-dependent midpoint centering of the second factor A7 code lowers frozen paid-image response error while retaining seven packed bitplanes; midpoint wins ten tested center rules.
limitation: Extra sign sums/corrections and min/max prep are unpaid natively; no composed language quality.
next: Measure full A7 reader and fit on quantized-producer composed loss.

title: First-stage A7 affine endpoints and stationary weight centers
summary: Sparse first-stage endpoint shifts barely help frozen codes; fitted stationary input-sum corrections lose held despite added payload and operations.
comparison: First-stage midpoint error layer 0 .017370 to .017359 but layer 27 .010931 to .010934; held-only weight-center oracle improves same-image RMS at most .43%.
limitation: Frozen image only; sparse corrections could matter with jointly trained codes.
next: Prioritize dynamic second-stage center and composed model fit.

title: Paid binary output scales and composed MLP gain
summary: Teacher-response scales already present in the packed up image lower held projection errors and improve a complete SiLU gate/up/down response after damaged upstream production.
comparison: On held damaged-producer inputs, up-scale fit lowers complete MLP RMS .610348 to .587859 at unchanged .520833 up BPW and factor work.
limitation: Gate/down remain original and FP64 replay is not full quantized model NLL or native time.
next: Fit paid scales with gate/down and actual quantized producer through gold loss.

title: Binary rank-order gauge
summary: Repacking paid one-bit factors by train energy changes A7 second-stage groups without changing their real product, bits or logical factor work.
comparison: Held RMS improves across four up layers, including layer 0 .017512 to .017419 and layer 27 .011547 to .011249.
limitation: Original-producer same-image response, no model quality or native latency.
next: Choose rank order with producer and full consumer jointly.

title: Frozen rank and sign-gauge searches
summary: Train-only rank swaps optimized for intermediate reconstruction or complete Gram response reverse on larger held panels; sign flips affect only rare asymmetric A7 cells.
comparison: Layer-14 held rank-pair safe fit .016117 to .016249; complete-Gram fit .015769 to .015817 on larger panel; sign-gauge changes RMS by millionths.
limitation: Rejects frozen search objectives, not new factor-code training.
next: Move selection to quantized-producer composed loss.

title: Frozen binary half-orbit selective preparation
summary: Nearly every frozen sign orbit is used, and fitting a 96-orbit cap loses the equal-fit 128-label quality control on both examined layers.
comparison: First plane occupies 62,285/65,536 and output plane 24,576/24,576; best selective preparation saves at most 3.64% Gray updates.
limitation: Only frozen signs or the tested capped fit, not learned direct-address alphabets.
next: Co-train factor signs under an addressable small alphabet if consumer work warrants it.

title: Paid A7 scalar threshold selection
summary: Two-boundary first/second factor thresholds improve complete frozen two-factor response without changing packed signs, scales or dot count.
comparison: Held layer-0/14 RMS .017775/.016480 to .017412/.016311 versus safe pair; first-only fit helps layer 0 .017775 to .017573.
limitation: Original-producer same-image result, no native time or whole-model quality.
next: Choose ladders against quantized-producer MLP/gold response.

title: Frozen per-group A7 threshold overfit
summary: Group-specific thresholds improve train response but lose held to one common first-stage selector.
comparison: Layer-0/14 held RMS .017360/.016066 to .017387/.016138 while adding 31 constants.
limitation: Only frozen signs, 128 train rows and fitted second threshold.
next: Fit group choices jointly with codes on complete model loss, if needed.
